questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was born in Norway and I really wanted to go back. Also, they have some nice academic opportunities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I am very happy with my study abroad as I gained a lot of experience

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I wasn't a problem at all

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: From the international department

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. I found housing through SIO and I was secured as an international student even before I went abroad

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I was staying in the northern part of Oslo and I studied in the city center. I bought a 30-days ticket at a time for public transportation and it made it all very easy. As long as the transportation method is cleared and done it's really not a problem living off campus!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was the same as at the University of Copenhagen. I was sent a login to their webpage 'Studentweb' where I registered for the semester and then I had to type in the courses I wished to take. As the registration for the courses opened up, I applied for the courses before the start of the semester. Then I waited until the final course registration was published.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help from the international department

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. The system was pretty much the same as the system at the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware of the deadlines for registration. Also, you can find most of the answers to your questions by looking up the homepage of the host university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses matched the level of courses at my home university.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was the same as at my home university. The courses were made of lectures and experimental exercises.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Terrestrisk zoologi and Norsk for internationale studerende

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the course 'Norsk for internationale studerende' for anyone going on an exchange in Norway. It's a great opportunity to get to learn more about the host country!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I was aware of the costs before the exchange.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Some food products were more expensive than I expected. I expected the ticket to the public transport to be more expensive than what it was. I was pleased with only paying 350 DK for a 30-day student ticket to travel by bus, metro and other public transport opportunities all around Oslo.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of opportunities for international students managed by all kinds of student organizations such as different athletic activities all week and also there were multiple Whats-app groups for social activities! I went on different hikes arranged by a group of international students and it was easy to get in touch with them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend getting into the different Whats-app and Facebook groups. I would personally recommend the social hikes around the city where the student is staying.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Again I would recommend getting on hikes/trips around the place where the student is staying. Also, I was staying with 5 other international students at 'SIO studenterby' and we had weekly eating-together-nights where we learned more about each other. It was a very nice way to spend the weekends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was not a problem as the norwegian and danish cultures are pretty much equal.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: As I was staying over the summer I went swimming at the local lake with a local student from my course. I had to be more extrovert and almost progressive as the local students (especially in Norway) are more or less focused in their own studies.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any cultural differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I found the local students to be very polite and I especially appreciated the staff at the host university as they were very helpful during my stay.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't be afraid - It will change your life for the good forever!
You have to be open and sometimes force yourself to be extra extrovert but only that way you can get to know other students over such a short period
Search up the housing opportunities at your host country as soon as possible

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to ask people around you for help!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I went back to the country where I was born, but other than that I was very pleased with the courses they have at the University of Oslo. I have gained a lot of experience and now I'm less scared to just jump into new things.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was to stay abroad by myself without my boyfriend haha

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
